comparator.name: International Bachelor Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme overview and 2026-2027 study schedule establish a 180-EC three-year bachelor with broad first- and second-year sequences in economics, business economics and quantitative methods. The third year contains 24 EC of minor/study-abroad/internship and elective space, 2 EC of Career Skills, a 24-EC major and a 10-EC individual thesis. The official major schedule lists nine majors but identifies no default or general route, so this reconstruction preserves the restricted 24-EC major choice generically rather than selecting a route for UCR convenience.
components: Minor / study abroad / internship / elective space
The official schedule permits a 12- or 15-EC minor, replaceable by study abroad or an internship, with the remaining 12 or 9 EC used for electives.

alternatives.label: Economics, business & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to International Economics and Business Economics combining markets, macroeconomics and policy with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisations, statistics, data and econometrics.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Behavioural & health economics, psychology & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics with behavioural science, psychology, public health, empirical methods, marketing and organisational decision-making; the label makes those substantive strands visible without implying a specialist health-economics degree.
alternatives.concept: A behavioural- and health-economics direction combining economic choice and policy with psychology, public health, experiments, consumer behaviour, marketing and empirical analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces advanced mathematics, probability, the AI-economy course, international business, consumer-product design and finance with brain-and-behaviour foundations, social psychology, medical and health psychology, epidemiology and public health, leadership communication and negotiation. The resulting curriculum retains economics, business and empirical analysis but organises them around human behaviour and health-related decisions.
progression: Economics, business, brain-and-behaviour, research and psychology foundations precede advanced microeconomics, public economics, medical and health psychology, organisational psychology, behavioural economics, econometrics and market research. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Medical & Health Psychology; Business Foundations precedes Market Research and Strategy & Digital Transformation; Research Methods & Statistics precedes the economics and business courses that require it. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics direction combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

candidates.label: Behavioural and health economics with consumer decisions

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the programme-wide economics, business and empirical core. Accounting was assessed but cannot support a distinct 24-course UCR programme because UCR has only one dedicated accounting course. The behavioural-and-health direction and the financial-economics direction each support coherent, feasible and substantively distinct curricula, so both are included. Markets, organisations and strategy are already substantively covered by the closest-match curriculum. International and policy economics remain defensible directions, but the maximum of three alternatives is reached; urban, port and transport economics is not feasible at UCR because the required specialist domain sequence is absent.

blocks: Both examine government intervention, redistribution, health-care provision and the trade-off between equity and efficiency; UCR Public Economics is broader than the comparator course.
The comparator contains a dedicated History of Economic Thought course. UCR does not add an unrelated history course merely to imitate this component.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations overlaps with organisation, markets and strategy but does not reproduce the comparator course in full.
Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis for business questions, but is not the same as the programme-wide Research Project.
International Business & Governance overlaps with international economic and institutional environments but is broader and more business-governance oriented.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistics and empirical research foundations, but is broader than Applied Statistics 1.
Linear Algebra directly covers matrix and vector methods in the comparator course, but not its full calculus, game-theory and linear-programming combination.
Personal & Professional Development overlaps with academic and professional formation but does not reproduce the comparator's economics-specific Academic Skills modules.
The comparator requires an individual 10-EC thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme provides a fixed two-year specialist sequence in economics, business economics and quantitative methods, followed by a formal major, seminar and individual thesis. UCR can build coherent economics-and-business, behavioural-and-health and finance-and-quantitative programmes, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or a dedicated Economics and Business Economics thesis.
